counterfactual_missing_items: No clear evidence of an alternative primary malignancy
No mention of a different type of skin cancer
No indication of an infectious or inflammatory process unrelated to melanoma
decisive_items: Incidentally resected lymph node showed focal involvement
H&E sections showed intense mixed superficial and deep dermal inflammatory infiltrate composed of numerous neutrophils, histiocytes, eosinophils, and lymphocytes
SOX-10 and MART-1: Highlighted normal melanocytes in basal layer of epidermis only
response.rationale: The champion, R6 (Melanoma), is supported by the patient's history of a scalp lesion, lymph node involvement, and satellite lesions, as well as the histopathology findings, including the presence of melanocytes on immunostaining. The runner-up, R5 (Recurrent Melanoma), is also a strong candidate, but R6 is more comprehensive, encompassing the overall diagnosis, while R5 focuses on the recurrence aspect.

rejected.why: While T-VEC therapy is mentioned, it is not the primary diagnosis, but rather a treatment the patient received.
The immune-mediated reaction is a possible mechanism, but it is not the primary diagnosis.
Tumor regression due to immunotherapy is an observed effect, but it is not the primary diagnosis.
